channel.title: The Berkshire Edge - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Berkshire Edge (theberkshireedge.com)

item.title: Berkshire Hills Regional School Committee approves proposed fiscal 2027 budget
item.description: The committee unanimously approved the budget despite objections from district teachers.

item.title: Berkshire County artists receive grants from Mass Cultural Council
item.description: This represents the largest annual investment in grants made to individuals in the agency's history, outside of the extraordinary one-time COVID-19 relief efforts.

item.title: Adams Theater sets 2026 lineup with dance, music, and literature
item.description: The season runs April through October and features national and local artists. The lineup includes dance, music, literature, and community events.

item.title: NATURE’S TURN: Snowbirds and other avian visitors come close to our homes
item.description: The dark-eyed junco, also known as slate-colored or northern junco, Junco hyemalis, is widely referred to as the “snowbird.”

item.title: I WITNESS: Fate of the union
item.description: One could sense the nationwide surge of gratitude as we learned that President Lies-a-Lot had fixed, in record time, everything that had plagued us in the past.

item.title: The digital erosion of childhood
item.description: When children spend their formative years staring at glass screens instead of human faces, they miss out on the critical development of mirror neurons, which are responsible for empathy.

item.title: The Olympics should be about more than chasing medals
item.description: Making your national team should be what it is about—while winning a medal of any color is just icing on the cake.

item.title: Berkshire Opera Festival presents Schubert’s ‘Winterreise’ on March 7 at Tanglewood’s Linde Center
item.description: Audiences still respond to Franz Schubert’s “Winterreise” nearly two centuries after it was composed because it speaks directly to experiences that never change: loss, isolation, and the search for meaning.

item.title: Poet of the Jazz Age . . . Langston Hughes
item.description: Hughes was born in Missouri and raised in Kansas. He was of mixed ancestry. But early on, Hughes chose to identify as black and throughout his life fought for racial equality and social justice.

item.title: THE OTHER SIDE: Alys Liu reclaims the ice
item.description: As Alysa Liu’s transcendence fades, I am left with the reality that there remains work to be done.
